title: Why production is needed

blocks.heading: Why production is needed
blocks.text: Production is the creation of goods and services that satisfy needs and wants. Producing useful goods and services connects available resources to human requirements; output alone does not establish that needs are met fairly. A good is a tangible product, such as a bag or a loaf. A service is an activity provided for someone, such as transport or teaching. Both are production. Making an item that no one can use does not by itself meet a need. Access, suitability and distribution affect whether people benefit.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Basic needs
blocks.text: A need is something essential for basic survival or well-being, such as adequate food, safe water or shelter. Meeting a basic need depends on access to a suitable good or service, not merely its existence. A settlement can have a water source yet lack safe access if the supply is contaminated or unaffordable. Explain the requirement being met: adequate food addresses nourishment, while shelter protects people from weather. Avoid defining need as whatever someone happens to buy.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Wants
blocks.text: A want is something a person would like beyond what is essential for basic survival or well-being. Needs and wants are distinguished by their purpose and circumstances rather than by whether an item costs money. Adequate clothing meets a need; an additional fashion accessory may meet a want. A particular item cannot be classified solely by its price. A communication device needed for a specified essential service may have a different role from another device bought as an optional upgrade.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: A production decision
blocks.text: An invented household needs adequate food but would also like decorative garden lights. Growing vegetables or providing food transport can contribute to the food need; making the lights meets a different want. Production can respond to both, but scarce time and resources require a choice. To explain why production is needed, name the requirement and show how the good or service meets it. A store full of food does not establish that a household can afford or reach it.
